request: Analyze GSE325919 for PMID 41911459 (Mitochondrial remodeling in skeletal muscle underlies exercise-induced reversal of age-associated functional decline in mice and humans.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk poly(A) RNA-seq, mouse gastrocnemius (S2.24.p1), RSEM expected counts on GRCm38 v91 (S2.24.p2)
final.sample_inclusion: 23-mo-old mice after a 10-wk HIMIT intervention started at 20 mo: WT untrained, WT trained, G6PD-Tg untrained; both sexes (S1.p1, S2.2.p1). GEO deposits 5 per group per sex = 30 samples (subset of the 61 mice phenotyped).
final.primary_estimand: Effect of 10-wk late-onset HIMIT exercise training on gastrocnemius gene expression in old (23 mo) WT mice: WT trained vs WT untrained (Fig. 2H comparison; S1.p7).
planned_contrasts: WT trained vs WT untrained (exercise effect; S1.p7, Fig. 2H; paper gives no DEG count in the text, results in Dataset S2 / SI Fig. S2E)
G6PD-Tg untrained vs WT untrained (transgene/robustness effect, not exercise; S1.p7, Fig. 2I)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none; one gastrocnemius sample per independent mouse
final.normalization: genes < 10 CPM filtered; expected counts TMM-normalised with edgeR (S2.24.p2)
final.paper_method: limma v3.50.3 on TMM-normalised RSEM expected counts (S2.24.p2); GSEA (clusterProfiler/DOSE, MitoCarta 3.0) at FDR q < 0.25 (S2.26.p3)
final.sex_handling: S2.26.p2: 'Sexes were analyzed separately' (general statistics statement; RNA-seq section does not say whether DE pooled sexes)

paper_threshold.note: no DEG threshold stated for RNA-seq; only GSEA FDR q < 0.25 (S2.26.p3)

final.paper_results: No DEG count or named DEG list in the main text; RNA-seq reported as GSEA of OxPhos, cristae formation, ROS detoxification and glutathione metabolism upregulated in trained and G6PD-Tg groups (S1.p7).

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Methods S2.24 define the RNA-seq route (RSEM expected counts -> CPM filter -> TMM (edgeR) -> limma). Results S1.p7 and Fig. 2H/I define the two comparisons against WT untrained. The paper states no DEG significance threshold; only the GSEA threshold FDR q < 0.25 (S2.26.p3). DEG counts live only in Dataset S2 (not available locally).

checks: S7.p1 names GSE325919 as the paper's RNA-seq deposit
GEO: Mus musculus muscle, polyA RNA, RSEM v1.3.1 on GRCm38 build 91 matches S2.24.p2
30 GSM samples: WT non-trained, WT trained, G6PD-tg non-trained x female/male (5 each), matching the paper's three groups
RAW.tar holds 30 RSEM *.genes.results.gz members, one per GSM; merged by prep_merge_rsem.py (expected_count column)

ownership.reasoning: Data availability statement S7.p1 and matching processing description.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns are GSM ids written by the prep script from the tar member names; exact match to the metadata index. Group and sex parsed from the GEO title (genotype column agrees).

matrix.reasoning: RSEM expected_count column (11% non-integer values), GEO data_processing: 'Expected expression counts ... Limma for normalization (using TMM method)'; paper S2.24.p2 uses the same expected counts as input. Not raw integer counts, so integer-only count methods are not used without a documented rounding recipe.

final.analysis_type: multigroup (one control, two treatment levels) with sex adjustment

design.reasoning: Three groups sharing one control (WT untrained); one model with planned contrasts, never pooled levels. Exercise estimand = TR vs SED; G6PD-Tg vs SED is the paper's second planned comparison but is a genotype effect, not exercise. Sex is balanced (5F/5M per group) and the paper analyses sexes separately (S2.26.p2), so the pooled model includes sex, and per-sex TR vs SED fits are added as exploratory (n = 5 vs 5).

candidates.value: grp only, sexes pooled without adjustment
candidates.reason_rejected: sex is a known major source of muscle expression variance and the paper treats sexes separately
RNA-seq methods do not state sex splitting; pooled sex-adjusted model is primary, per-sex fits kept as exploratory

covariates.name: sex
covariates.disposition: fixed effect in the pooled model; balanced across groups

covariance.reasoning: Independent animals, one sample each; no batch or lane recorded in GEO. Sex is a design factor of the study (both sexes, S2.2.p1) and balanced 5/5 in every group, so it is adjusted, not confounded.

final.method: limma (moderated t, eBayes) on log2(CPM+1) of RSEM expected counts

paper_route.method: edgeR TMM normalisation + limma on expected counts after <10 CPM filter
paper_route.reason: runner has no TMM normalisation or CPM-based filter for limma; voom/edgeR require integers and the paper documents no rounding of expected counts

deviations: library-size CPM (no TMM factors) instead of TMM
low-expression filter = count >= 10 in >= 3 samples (preprocess_counts) instead of the paper's < 10 CPM filter
sex included as a covariate in the pooled model (paper RNA-seq handling of sex not stated)

method.reasoning: Paper used limma on TMM-normalised expected counts (S2.24.p2). The closest validated route for estimated counts without rounding is limma on log2(CPM+1); declared deviation.

paper_threshold.note: no DEG threshold stated for RNA-seq; only GSEA FDR q < 0.25 (S2.26.p3)

threshold.reasoning: The paper states no DEG threshold for RNA-seq (S2.24.p2, S2.26.p3 gives only GSEA FDR q < 0.25 and general P < 0.05 for physiological tests). Workflow default BH padj < 0.05, no fold-change rule; raw p < 0.05 kept as a labelled audit count.

caveats: paper DEG counts are only in Dataset S2 (not available); no count comparison possible
GSEA in the paper used MitoCarta 3.0 sets; here MSigDB Hallmark GSEA is run as a qualitative check of the OxPhos direction
G6PD-Tg vs WT untrained is a genotype contrast, not an exercise effect

study.reasoning: Method deviates (no TMM, different filter); threshold is workflow default because the paper gives none.

discrepancies.paper: WT untrained n = 21, WT trained n = 20, G6PD-Tg n = 20 phenotyped (S1.p1)
discrepancies.data: RNA-seq subset 5 per group per sex (30 samples)
runner offers library-size log2(CPM+1) with count >= 10 in >= 3 samples filter
pooled sex-adjusted model primary; per-sex exploratory fits added

executions.name: joint
executions.reasoning: One limma model ~ sex + grp on all 30 samples; planned contrasts TR vs SED (exercise, primary) and G6PD vs SED (secondary).

executions.name: TR_vs_SED_female
executions.reasoning: Paper analyses sexes separately (S2.26.p2); female exercise effect, n = 5 vs 5.

enrichment.reasoning: Paper reports GSEA of OxPhos/mitochondrial programmes for trained vs untrained (S1.p7, S2.26.p3); Hallmark GSEA on the full ranking checks the direction.
Paper reports the same OxPhos enrichment for G6PD-Tg vs WT untrained (S1.p7).
